title: The First Vision Narrative
notes: Primary documents: multiple accounts of the First Vision (1832, 1835, 1838, 1842)

footnotes.text: Orson Pratt,A Interesting Account of Several Remarkable Visions and of the Late Discovery of Ancient American Records (Edinburgh: Ballantyne and Hughes, 1840), 4, Church History Library, Salt Lake City; josephsmithpapers.org.

Joseph Smith, interview by David Nye White, Aug. 21, 1843, in David Nye White, “The Prairies, Nauvoo, Joe Smith, the Temple, the Mormons, &c,” Pittsburg Weekly Gazette, Sept. 15, 1843, 3, Church History Library; josephsmithpapers.org.

Orson Hyde,Ein Ruf aus der Wüste (A Cry out of the Wilderness), 14–15, Church History Library; josephsmithpapers.org. The word “distracting” could also be translated as “unfitting” or “discordant.” It has also been translated as “inappropriate.”
See Orson Pratt,A Interesting Account of Several Remarkable Visions, 5; see also Joseph Smith, “History, circa Summer 1832,” 2;Alexander Neibaur journal, May 24, 1844.

Joseph Smith, “Church History,” inTimes and Seasons, vol. 3, no. 9 (Mar. 1, 1842), 707, Church History Library; josephsmithpapers.org. In his first writing of the experience, he simply used the wordLordto describe these two glorious beings.
Levi Richards journal, June 11, 1843, Church History Library; josephsmithpapers.org.
